questions.question: Which mythological hero is known for his journey to the underworld to retrieve his deceased wife Eurydice?
questions.explanation: Orpheus is a central figure in Greek mythology, whose story revolves around loss and the power of music. His journey to the underworld is one of the most famous narratives in which he attempts to outsmart death to bring Eurydice back to life.

choices: Which of the following tea styles is known for its preparation with a special tea folded in a bowl and is often considered part of a ceremonial practice in Japan?

questions.question: Matcha is a powdered green tea that plays a central role in Japanese tea art. The preparation involves whisking the powder with hot water in a special bowl, resulting in a frothy consistency. This style is often associated with traditional ceremonies.
choices: Which of these cities is simultaneously the capital of the eponymous city-state?

questions.question: Nicosia is the capital of the city-state of Cyprus. It is the only divided capital in Europe and plays an important role in the political and cultural life of the country.
choices: Which organ of Athenian democracy was responsible for legislation?

questions.question: The People's Assembly, also known as the Ecclesia, was the central organ of Athenian democracy where all citizens had the right to enact laws and decide on important political matters. It played a crucial role in the political participation of the citizens of Athens in the 5th century BC.

Which writer coined the phrase 'Thoughts are free' and thereby addressed the freedom of thought in his works?

questions.question: The phrase 'Thoughts are free' was popularized by Heinrich Heine, who frequently addressed the themes of freedom and self-determination in his poems. This idea is found in various contexts of German literature, especially in the 19th century, when the pursuit of individual freedom and political emancipation was strongly emphasized.
choices: Which process primarily describes the conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into a bioavailable form by microorganisms in aquatic ecosystems?

questions.question: Nitrogen fixation is the process by which microbes convert nitrogen from the atmosphere into a form usable by plants. This is particularly important in aquatic ecosystems where nitrogen is often a limiting nutrient.

choices: Which of the following distances is commonly used in competitive swimming for freestyle and medley races?

The 100-meter distance is one of the most common distances in competitive swimming for freestyle and medley races. This distance is often swum in various competitions and championships, making it a well-known measure in aquatics.

questions.question: A: 1500 meters

choices: Which theory explains how species change and adapt to their environment over long periods of time?

The theory of evolution describes the process by which organisms change over time to better adapt to their environment. This occurs through natural selection, where the best-adapted individuals have more offspring.
